frame: RESOURCE comparison (two-copy primitive vs the tomography block it replaces), NOT a quantum-advantage claim; classical shadows estimate purity with no 2nd copy.
scope: primitive-level head-to-head, not a named-grader retrofit.
estimators:
two-copy: unbiased per-shot (-1)^(sum u&v); tomography: unbiased variance-subtracted (1/2^n)sum(

^2 - Var).
headline: MEASURED shot-bill is a WASH at n<=3: two-copy vs tomography-block matched-SE ratio = 1.22x / 0.66x / 0.86x (n=1/2/3) -> two-copy is NOT cheaper in total shots; tomography marginally ahead at n=2,3. The 3^n->1 settings reduction is a real OPERATIONAL difference but converts to NO shot saving in this window.
why_wash: Two-copy per-shot variance = 1 - purity^2 (n-independent): predicted 0.595/0.855/0.911 vs measured 0.598/0.847/0.926. The fixed states are LOW purity (0.636/0.381/0.299), inflating two-copy variance toward 1, while tomography at only 3/9/27 settings is still cheap. The asymptotic two-copy shot advantage is real but needs larger n or higher purity; n<=3 does not reach the crossover. NOTE: the decreasing-purity state choice DISFAVORED two-copy, so this wash is pessimistic-for-two-copy, not a rigged baseline.
accuracy_note: Both arms recover the true purity but at n=3 both read LOW (two-copy 0.273 = 1.7sigma; tomography 0.291 = 2.7sigma on its tiny 0.0027 SE) — a hardware-decoherence systematic pulling measured correlations down. SE bars are STATISTICAL-ONLY (do not include this systematic).
followup: A higher-n or higher-purity flight would reach the two-copy shot-advantage crossover — named, not launched (Creator asked for §3(b), delivered).
